_comment: Each entry describes one authoritative service, the exact query sent to it,
and which normalizer converts its rows into UniMap records.
IMPORTANT: the 'attribution' and 'terms' strings below were written without
network access and could NOT be checked against each service's current terms
page. Confirm them before publishing a catalogue built from these sources.
The '{limit}' placeholder in a query is replaced with the --limit value, or
removed entirely when no limit is given.
The '{identifiers}' placeholder is replaced with the source's
'select_identifiers' list, quoted and comma-joined, so a curated query asks
the service only for the objects UniMap actually wants. This keeps curated
imports small and polite instead of downloading a whole catalogue and
A source marked '"unprobed": true' has never had its real response
inspected. The importer refuses to import from it and allows only --probe.
Probe it, read the actual columns, write or correct its normalizer, then
remove the flag. Do not guess column names.

sources.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive
sources.attribution: This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program.
sources.terms: Public domain / open access. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.query: select {limit} pl_name, hostname, sy_dist, pl_rade, pl_bmasse, disc_year, discoverymethod, ra, dec from pscomppars where sy_dist is not null and pl_rade is not null order by sy_dist asc, pl_name asc

sources.name: SIMBAD (CDS, Strasbourg)
sources.attribution: This research has made use of the SIMBAD database, operated at CDS, Strasbourg, France.
sources.terms: Attribution required; bulk querying discouraged. Use modest limits. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: Restricted to objects with a measured parallax so distance is derived from a published value rather than estimated. SIMBAD's basic table carries no radius, so these records have no size/circumference.
sources.note_unprobed: SIMBAD has never returned a response to this project. The 2026-07-26 attempt failed on a local trust store (CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED) and the 2026-07-26 retry failed at the network policy (403 CONNECT). The column names below are assumptions taken from SIMBAD's documented 'basic' table and are NOT confirmed. Probe before importing.
sources.query: select {limit} main_id, ra, dec, plx_value, otype_txt, sp_type from basic where otype_txt = 'Star' and plx_value > 20 and ra is not null and dec is not null order by plx_value desc, main_id asc

sources.name: SIMBAD (CDS, Strasbourg)
sources.attribution: This research has made use of the SIMBAD database, operated at CDS, Strasbourg, France.
sources.terms: Attribution required; bulk querying discouraged. Use modest limits. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: Curated named stars rather than a parallax-ordered sweep: the brightest naked-eye stars, the nearest stars, famous variables and supergiants, and well-known exoplanet host stars. Selecting WHICH stars to carry is an editorial decision recorded here; every value in the resulting record still comes from SIMBAD. A name that SIMBAD does not resolve simply produces no record - it is never filled in from memory.
sources.note_unprobed: Joins 'ident' to 'basic' to match on any catalogued identifier rather than on main_id alone. Both the join column (oidref/oid) and the selected columns are assumptions and are NOT confirmed. Probe before importing.
sources.note_distance: Distance is derived from the published parallax as 1000/plx parsecs. Stars without a parallax in SIMBAD yield no distance and are skipped, which is correct: an invented distance is worse than an absent star.
sources.target_count: 40-60 stars in the final catalogue, including the 4 already present.
sources.query: select {limit} b.main_id, b.ra, b.dec, b.plx_value, b.otype_txt, b.sp_type from basic as b join ident as i on b.oid = i.oidref where i.id in ({identifiers})

sources.name: SIMBAD (CDS, Strasbourg)
sources.attribution: This research has made use of the SIMBAD database, operated at CDS, Strasbourg, France.
sources.terms: Attribution required; bulk querying discouraged. Use modest limits. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: Curated Messier/NGC/IC galaxies plus the Magellanic Clouds. Editorial selection only; all values come from SIMBAD.
sources.note_unprobed: The simbad_deep_sky normalizer does not exist yet and must not be written from assumptions. Galaxy distances are NOT parallaxes - SIMBAD's basic table has no distance column, so the distance must come from a confirmed field (the 'mesDistance' table is the likely candidate) whose name, units and semantics have to be read off a real probe. Probe first, then write the normalizer.
sources.target_count: 20-30 galaxies in the final catalogue, including the 4 already present.
sources.query: select {limit} b.main_id, b.ra, b.dec, b.otype_txt from basic as b join ident as i on b.oid = i.oidref where i.id in ({identifiers})

sources.name: SIMBAD (CDS, Strasbourg)
sources.attribution: This research has made use of the SIMBAD database, operated at CDS, Strasbourg, France.
sources.terms: Attribution required; bulk querying discouraged. Use modest limits. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: Curated emission, reflection, planetary and supernova-remnant nebulae.
sources.note_classification: This list deliberately mixes several SIMBAD object types. M 1 is a supernova remnant that also hosts the Crab pulsar; NGC 6960 and NGC 6992 are parts of one remnant. The normalizer must map SIMBAD's real otype value onto a UniMap type rather than stamping every row 'Nebula', or the catalogue will assert classifications the source does not support. That mapping cannot be written until a probe shows the actual otype strings.
sources.target_count: 20-30 nebulae in the final catalogue, including the 3 already present.
sources.query: select {limit} b.main_id, b.ra, b.dec, b.otype_txt from basic as b join ident as i on b.oid = i.oidref where i.id in ({identifiers})

sources.name: SIMBAD (CDS, Strasbourg)
sources.attribution: This research has made use of the SIMBAD database, operated at CDS, Strasbourg, France.
sources.terms: Attribution required; bulk querying discouraged. Use modest limits. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: Curated pulsars and isolated neutron stars of historical or educational importance: the first pulsar discovered, the first binary pulsar, the first pulsar planets, the Crab and Vela pulsars, a magnetar and a fast millisecond pulsar.
sources.note_classification: SIMBAD distinguishes pulsars from neutron stars. UniMap now accepts both 'Neutron Star' and 'Pulsar' types and reaches them through one 'Neutron Stars' filter. The normalizer must take the type from the source's otype, not from this list's intent.
sources.target_count: 10-15 neutron stars and pulsars in the final catalogue, including the 2 already present.
sources.query: select {limit} b.main_id, b.ra, b.dec, b.otype_txt from basic as b join ident as i on b.oid = i.oidref where i.id in ({identifiers})

sources.name: SIMBAD (CDS, Strasbourg)
sources.attribution: This research has made use of the SIMBAD database, operated at CDS, Strasbourg, France.
sources.terms: Attribution required; bulk querying discouraged. Use modest limits. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: Curated stellar-mass X-ray binaries and supermassive black holes.
sources.note_classification: This is the least certain of the curated sets and may not be importable as-is. SIMBAD generally types these objects by what is observed - 'HighMassXBin', 'LowMassXBin', 'AGN', 'Seyfert' - rather than as black holes, because the black hole is an inference from the system's dynamics. Stamping every row 'Black Hole' would assert a classification the source does not make. If the probe confirms that, the honest options are to carry them under their observed type or to leave black holes out of the automated import and curate them by hand against a named published measurement. Decide after the probe; do not force the category.
sources.target_count: 10-15 black holes in the final catalogue, including the 3 already present.
sources.query: select {limit} b.main_id, b.ra, b.dec, b.otype_txt from basic as b join ident as i on b.oid = i.oidref where i.id in ({identifiers})

sources.name: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database
sources.attribution: Data courtesy of NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics, Small-Body Database.
sources.terms: Public domain, attribution appreciated. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: sb-class=TNO returns every trans-Neptunian object, most of which are small bodies and NOT dwarf planets. select_names therefore restricts the import to the IAU-recognised trans-Neptunian dwarf planets. Widening this list is an editorial decision, not a query change. Ceres is a main-belt object and is not covered by this source entry.
sources.note_distance: Solar-system 'distance' is a mean orbital distance in AU, a different quantity from the light-year distances used for deep-sky objects. The record labels it explicitly.

sources.name: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database
sources.attribution: Data courtesy of NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics, Small-Body Database.
sources.terms: Public domain, attribution appreciated. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: Ceres alone, by design. Ceres is a main-belt object, so the sb-class=TNO query that supplies the other four dwarf planets cannot reach it. This is a single-object lookup rather than a widened class query: broadening it to 'sb-class=AST' would return hundreds of thousands of asteroids that are not dwarf planets, which is exactly the mistake the TNO curation filter exists to prevent.
sources.note_unprobed: This is a DIFFERENT endpoint from sbdb_query.api, not a different query against the same one. sbdb.api is documented to return a nested object ({object, orbit, phys_par}) rather than the {fields, data} table shape, so rows_from_payload cannot read it and jpl_sbdb cannot normalize it. Its normalizer is deliberately null: it must be written against a real probe, after confirming object identity, the classification string, which field carries the semi-major axis, which carries the diameter, what units each uses, and what aliases the object record lists. Probe first.

sources.name: NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics — Planetary Satellite Physical Parameters
sources.attribution: Data courtesy of NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics.
sources.terms: Public domain, attribution appreciated. CONFIRM before publishing.
sources.note: Curated major planetary satellites: the Galilean moons, the large Saturnian moons, Triton, Charon, the Martian moons, and the five major Uranian moons.
sources.note_distance: Moon 'distance' is a different quantity again - an orbital distance from its PARENT PLANET, not from the Sun and not from Earth. It must be labelled with the parent body or it is actively misleading next to a galaxy's light-year distance. Confirm on the probe whether this endpoint carries orbital radius at all; the physical-parameters table may supply only radius, mass and density, in which case the orbital distance has to come from a second endpoint or moons wait for the next slice.
sources.note_unprobed: Endpoint, response shape and field names are all unconfirmed. No normalizer is written. Probe first.
sources.target_count: 15-25 moons, only if the probe shows a usable distance semantic.
